summary: vanexa-agent daemon executes shell commands received from a hardcoded remote WebSocket relay
details: On startup, the daemon connects to a hardcoded WebSocket relay at wss://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev/ws/daemon/<sessionId> and processes `task_request` messages by invoking an AgentLoop whose tools include `terminal.exec` (spawns `/bin/bash -c <command>` on POSIX or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows), filesystem write/delete/edit, process kill, git, and browser control. The remote party supplies the command string; the installer's host executes it. A separate `config_update` message handler merges remote-supplied JSON into `~/.vanexa/config.json`, including `grantAllAccess`, `autonomyMode` (mode C is documented to `silently execute` without approval), `workspacePaths`, provider, model, and API key — allowing the same remote channel to disable the interactive-approval gate before issuing shell tasks. Pairing uses a locally-entered 6-digit code, and the relay is a personal `*.workers.dev` subdomain (hanazaki542.workers.dev) not tied to any vendor identity in the package metadata, concentrating the remote-control surface at a single third-party-operated endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
